title: Act II, Scene I

teacherSummary.text: Polonius sends Reynaldo to Paris to spy on Laertes by spreading small slanders. Ophelia enters frightened: Hamlet came to her closet dishevelled, stared, sighed and left. Polonius concludes Hamlet is mad for love and goes to tell the king.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “O, my lord, my lord, I have been so affrighted” slowly and put it in my own words: Ophelia tells her father that she has been terribly frightened by Hamlet. Next, craft. I notice the repeated "my lord, my lord," which shows breathless fear. The strongest word is “affrighted”: an old, stronger form of "afraid," it shows real shock. Then, effect. Why is Ophelia so frightened? My answer: Ophelia is frightened because Hamlet burst into her room disheveled, pale and silent, staring at her; Polonius takes it as love-madness, while we suspect an act or real distress.
